channel.title: Throttle blog
channel.description: Measuring what self-hosted LLM inference really costs.

item.title: FP8 looked 47% cheaper. It wasn't.
item.description: vLLM's on-the-fly FP8 made a 72B model look 47% cheaper per token and a 32B look 41% cheaper. Both times the answers had changed shape; the 32B answered "!!!!". The FP8 checkpoint that really did cut 32%, and the check I run before trusting any FP8 saving.

item.title: Your second GPU might be costing you 28% more per token
item.description: Qwen2.5-72B on rented AMD MI300X: one GPU cost $1.67 per million output tokens, two GPUs with tensor parallelism cost $2.14. 1.56x the throughput, 28% more per token. The run, the arithmetic, and when a second GPU is still worth it.

item.title: I changed nothing and my LLM server got 27% more expensive
item.description: Four cost checks of the same untouched Ollama server came back at $8.77, $8.86, $11.26 and $10.02 per million output tokens. Why same-server runs swing, and the noise bound I now use before believing any before/after number.

item.title: How to measure cost per million tokens on a self-hosted LLM (vLLM, SGLang, Ollama)
item.description: A practical guide to turning GPU dollars per hour into dollars per million tokens for vLLM, SGLang and Ollama, the four pitfalls that make the number wrong, and how to re-check it after every config change and in CI.

item.title: One vLLM flag, −68.6% cost per token: what a counterbalanced benchmark looks like
item.description: A real A100 run where changing vLLM's max_num_seqs from 1 to 8 took cost from $0.746 to $0.234 per million output tokens, measured with a six-position B-C-B / C-B-C protocol. How the protocol works, the raw numbers, and what the result does not mean.
